answer: Each agent may submit a claim, but only claims backed by a costly, nontransferable stake enter the kernel’s reputation ledger. A random sample of interactions is audited; proven fraud burns the stake and removes the claim’s accumulated reputation, while honest service slowly earns it back. Cloning identities therefore does not multiply influence: every clone needs fresh capital and must survive the same audits. An umber-market newcomer can still earn standing, but cannot cheaply flood the haven with disposable personas.
